label: UniFi Ultra
description: UniFi Ultra (USW-Ultra) - 8x 1G RJ45 (1G/100M/10M): 7 PoE+ PSE ports (30 W/port) plus 1 PoE++ input port that powers the switch. No PoE budget without a power source: 42 W on PoE++ input, 16 W on PoE+ input, 52 W with the 60 W AC adapter, 202 W with the 210 W AC adapter. 16 Gbps switching capacity.

poe.note: 42 W models this SKU's own powering: the base unit is offered with 'No AC Adapter' and is powered by PoE++ from an upstream switch, dropping to 16 W if only PoE+ is available. Ubiquiti publishes PoE availability as a function of how the unit is powered, not as one number. techspecs 'Total PoE Availability': PoE++ input 42 W, PoE+ input 16 W, 60 W PoE adapter input 42 W, 60 W AC adapter input 52 W, 210 W AC adapter input 202 W. Max. PoE Output is PoE+ (30 W per port by PSE), so no port sources 802.3bt: port 8 of the 8 RJ45 is a PoE++ INPUT for powering the switch, and the store page states 'PoE input is supported for switch operation, with PoE+/PoE++ input or AC power required for PoE output'. The 60W/210W/60W-PoE-adapter rows are configurations of the same chassis, so a lab that powers this unit from a different adapter inherits that row, not this one. Port ceilings now carried per port: techspecs 'PoE Ports: PoE+ 7' and 'Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE: PoE+ 30W' (read 2026-11-21), so eth0-eth6 declare 30 W each instead of the bare direction bit, which the engine reads as 1 W.
